## $x_1$ seams between blocks (`layout: cubed`, `nb1` > 1) {#sec-ch03-x1seams}

Only the `cubed` layout splits $x_1$ (@sec-ch03-layouts). The vertical schemes of @sec-ch05 are column operations: the
hydrostatic reference is a scan from the top of the column, and several switches read windows that reach past a block
edge. Four mechanisms make a split column match one block. (a) The reference scan is relayed from the top block down,
each block passing its bottom face value to the block below. (b) The reference ghost rows are overwritten with the
neighbour's interior rows. (c) Switch-specific ghost rows past the seam are the neighbour's: the primitive ghost
layers under `dynamics.conversion-order: 4`, the plain-mean ghost cells under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`, the face
pressures, the $x_2$ and $x_3$ face states one row past the seam under the face-flux covariance (on by default), for
the hydro and for the scalars, and the density increment one row past it under `gravity-work: face`. (d) On every
$x_1$ seam the seam-face flux, with its face pressure and pressure base, is replaced by the mean of the two sides.
Wall reconstructions and wall mirroring are gated on a physical face, so they never act at a seam; column-wide
EOS[^rg-b43b7aad09b4] repairs gather the whole column. Every relay is one call of the one seam transport: the column's
two faces are the seam sides 0 (below) and 1 (above) of dimension 1, as the panel seams of @sec-ch03-seamreg are the
sides of dimensions 2 and 3.

Local symbols: $\mathrm{sm}$ (upright) an $x_1$ seam face shared by the block below ($\mathrm{B}$) and above
($\mathrm{T}$); $\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{sm}}$, $\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_{\mathrm{sm}}$ the $x_1$ fluxes the two blocks compute there;
$p^{\mathrm{top}}$ the reference face pressure a block receives at its upper face; $A_{\mathrm{sm}}$ the area of the seam face
[$\mathrm{m^2}$].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** A column split into several $x_1$ blocks behaves like one block: the hydrostatic reference scan is
relayed down the column, reference ghost rows are the neighbour's interior rows, switch-specific ghost rows are
exchanged, and the seam flux is averaged (@eq-ch03-x1seams-average).

**Data.** In/out: reference rows, switch-specific ghost rows and seam fluxes, in their own units.

**Placement.** Each stage: the relay when the reconstruction builds its $x_1$ reference; the flux average after the
$x_1$ fluxes, on the register's total and kept rows, the face pressure and the pressure base.

**Activation.** YAML `distribute: {layout: cubed, nb1}` with `nb1` > 1; default off (`nb1: 1`). Requires
`nghost` $\ge 3$ with gravity under `conversion-order: 4` or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`; blocks of one process must run
concurrently; no capture and no implicit solve.

**Guarantee / limits.** Round-off agreement with one block ($10^{-13}$ relative in the tests), not bitwise.

**Evidence.** `test_x1_seam_split` and its arms, `test_x1_seam_split_mp` and its arms, `test_pref_local_seam`,
`test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp` (pass at the pin); check `[C13]`.
:::

### Derivation

**Single-valued seam flux.** Let $V_{\mathrm B}$ and $V_{\mathrm T}$ be the volumes of the two cells that share the
seam, the top cell of block B and the bottom cell of block T [$\mathrm{m^3}$]. Block B updates its top cell with
$-A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{sm}}/V_{\mathrm B}$ and block T its bottom cell with $+A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_{\mathrm{sm}}/V_{\mathrm T}$, per
unit time. Multiplying each update by its own volume and by $\Delta t$[^rg-6e5d28d7b425] gives the change of the column total at the
seam per stage:

$$
V_{\mathrm B}\left(-\frac{A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm B}_{\mathrm{sm}}}{V_{\mathrm B}}\right)\Delta t
+ V_{\mathrm T}\left(\frac{A_{\mathrm{sm}}\mathbf F^{\mathrm T}_{\mathrm{sm}}}{V_{\mathrm T}}\right)\Delta t
= A_{\mathrm{sm}}\left(\mathbf F^{\mathrm T}_{\mathrm{sm}} - \mathbf F^{\mathrm B}_{\mathrm{sm}}\right)\Delta t ,
$$

zero only if the two agree. Both blocks replace their value by

$$
\bar{\mathbf F}_{\mathrm{sm}} = \tfrac12\left(\mathbf F^{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{sm}} + \mathbf F^{\mathrm{T}}_{\mathrm{sm}}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch03-x1seams-average}

and floating-point addition is commutative, so both hold the same bits and the sums telescope exactly across the seam.
@eq-ch03-x1seams-average is the register's `SeamRule::mean`, applied by `FluxRegister::replace` to the seam faces of
the total and of each kept part ({{< code src/hydro/flux_register.hpp FluxRegister::replace >}}); the face pressure
and the pressure base, which are not register rows, are averaged beside it
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}). It runs on every $x_1$ seam, between processes and
inside one process alike, a periodic wrap included.

**Reference relay.** The default reference is a scan of face pressures down from an anchor at the top of the column,
each cell adding its own hydrostatic drop. Split into blocks, each block needs as anchor the face value the scan has
reached at its upper face. The top block anchors itself; each other block takes $p^{\mathrm{top}}$ from the block above
and, after its own scan, passes its bottom face value down (`take_anchor` and `pass_anchor` of `ExchangeX1Link`,
{{< code src/recon/x1_reference.cpp ExchangeX1Link::take_anchor >}}). The relay is serial from top to bottom, so every
block's anchor equals the value the one-block scan has at the same face, up to the order of the additions. The scan
kernel itself is in @sec-ch05.

**Ghost rows.** A block's ghost rows of the reference computed locally from its ghost quadrature differ from the
owner's interior values. Replacing them by the neighbour's interior rows, through `exchange_ghost_rows`
({{< code src/recon/x1_reference.cpp ExchangeX1Link::exchange_ghost_rows >}}), makes the perturbation field
identical on both sides of the seam. Nothing in the derivation is truncated; the remaining differences from one block
are round-off from the order of operations.

The check takes the seam average on $4\times10^5$ random pairs with the two operands in both orders: the
two blocks' results carry identical bit patterns, and the seam's contribution to the column total is exactly zero
at every pair. Without the average the same seam leaves a non-zero residual at every pair, up to
$9.1\times10^3$ in flux units, which is the term @eq-ch03-x1seams-average removes (`[C13]`).[^x1s-c13] The relay
and the ghost rows are covered by the tests below.

[^x1s-c13]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C13]`; a numpy port of the $x_1$ seam-face average (at 73c45a7c the register's `SeamRule::mean`), CPU,
    double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

All four mechanisms run in every stage of a split column. The relay and the reference ghost rows run when the
reconstruction builds its $x_1$ reference; the switch ghost rows before the reconstruction that reads them; the seam
average after the $x_1$ fluxes are computed and before the positivity limiter; the face-pressure ghost rows after the
average. Each relay is a call of `Exchange` ({{< code src/layout/exchange.cpp Exchange::x1_rows >}}): `x1_rows`
packs $m$ rows from below the top face (up) and from above the bottom face (down), hands the two seam sides to
`seam_exchange`, and copies the neighbour's rows into its ghosts; `x1_seam_slab`
({{< code src/layout/exchange.cpp Exchange::x1_seam_slab >}}) moves the seam-face slab. A same-process neighbour is
reached through an in-memory board, a remote one through the process group (@sec-ch14). The neighbours are
`x1_neighbors` for the relays, which has none on a periodic $x_1$ column, and `x1_seam_peers` for the flux average
({{< code src/layout/exchange.cpp Exchange::x1_seam_peers >}}). The message tags are the `ExchangeTag` values
({{< code src/layout/exchange.hpp ExchangeTag >}}): 0x7715 (the reference anchor), 0x7717 (its ghost rows), 0x7720
(the seam flux), 0x7722 (face pressures), 0x7724 (plain means), 0x7726 (the density increment of the face gravity
work), 0x772a (primitive ghost layers), 0x7730 and 0x7734 (the $x_2$ and $x_3$ covariance face states), and
`0x7740 + 4k` for scalar row $k$[^rg-2dedcdaf1d1e]; the up message carries the tag and the down message the tag plus
one. EOS column repairs call `gather_x1`, which joins the column's pieces bottom first. @fig-ch03-x1seams-relay shows
a column of three blocks.

```{python}

#| fig-cap: "A column split into three $x_1$ blocks. Black arrows: the reference relay, top block to bottom block, one face value per seam. Purple arrows: each block's interior rows copied into the neighbour's ghost rows. At each seam face the two one-sided fluxes (orange) are replaced by their mean."
#| fig-alt: "Three stacked blocks with downward arrows at the seams, short arrows into hatched ghost rows, and paired flux arrows at each seam face."
```

: Code map of the $x_1$ seams. {#tbl-ch03-x1seams-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-x1seams-code):

1. Setup refuses `dynamics.conversion-order: 4` or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` with gravity and `nghost` < 3
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. In the stage, the switch ghost rows come from the neighbours through `x1_rows`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).
3. The reference evaluation takes the anchor from above, scans, passes its bottom face down, and swaps its ghost rows
   with both neighbours ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_hydro_ref_x1 >}}).
4. After the $x_1$ fluxes, every seam face is averaged with `x1_seam_slab` and `replace(1, faces, peer,
   SeamRule::mean)`, then the face-pressure ghost rows past the seam are exchanged with `x1_rows`
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it.** A column split into two blocks held by one process:

```yaml
distribute: {layout: cubed, nb1: 2, blocks_per_process: 2}   # build through Mesh; the blocks run concurrently
```

Refused:

- `nb1` > 1 on another layout ("SlabLayoutImpl: pz must be 1 for slab layout");
- with gravity, `conversion-order: 4` or `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` with `nghost` < 3 ("SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT (or
  dynamics/conversion-order 4) needs nghost >= 3, got 2");
- an implicit scheme ("[Hydro] implicit scheme requires nb1 = 1 (no x1 decomposition): the vertical solve has no
  cross-rank coupling.");
- more than 16 blocks per process when blocks exchange with another process ("[Layout:send_to_block] at most 16 blocks per process").

A split column also runs eager: the stage executor records "an x1 split (pz > 1): its relays inside the stage are
not cut into segments yet" among its refusals and does not capture (@sec-ch14). The seam average
@eq-ch03-x1seams-average is ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
    if (!options->disable_flux_x1() && playout && playout->options->nb(1) > 1) {
      Exchange ex(pmb);
      auto [below, above] = ex.x1_seam_peers(/*process_only=*/false);
      if (above >= 0 || below >= 0) {
    ...
        auto [from_below, from_above] =
            ex.x1_seam_slab(dn_mine, up_mine, kTagSeamFlux, false);
    ...
        freg.replace(1, faces, peer, SeamRule::mean);
```

The reference cases are `local_blocks_restart_the_reference_at_the_seam` ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp HydroRefX1.local_blocks_restart_the_reference_at_the_seam >}}) and
`in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps` ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp HydroRefX1.in_process_split_matches_one_block_after_200_steps >}}). The arms run one
gtest each with their environment through the CMake function `seam_arm` ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}); the
comparisons are in `split_gap` and its callers ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp split_gap >}}). With
`gravity-work: face`, `radial_exact_split_gap` ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp radial_exact_split_gap >}})
bounds both the split column's gap to one block and its drift of $\mathcal E=\sum_iV_iE_i+P$ (appendix A, notation
group 5) by $10^{-13}$, for 32, 64 and 128 cells. The seam-side case is `the_x1_relays_are_seam_sides`
({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.the_x1_relays_are_seam_sides >}}). CUDA twins of three arms
(`_x1_centroid_cuda`, `_radial_exact_cuda`, `_co4_face_density_cuda`) are registered by `seam_arm` when CUDA is built;
the `_mp` entries run on two processes. At the pin all 16 `test_x1_seam_split*` entries (12 in one process, the CUDA twins on a GPU, and 4 on two
processes) pass,
and so do `test_pref_local_seam.release` and `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp.release`.[^x1s-run]

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Blocks of one process in a split column must run concurrently; a block waits at most 5 minutes for its anchor.
- At most 16 blocks per process can exchange block messages.
- A split column is not captured, and an implicit scheme refuses it.
- A periodic $x_1$ column has no relay neighbours (`x1_neighbors`), so its block edges keep one-sided slopes in the
  face gravity work; setup warns that $-g_1x_1$ jumps at the periodic face ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
:::

A split column is not bitwise equal to one block; the tests use $10^{-13}$ and $10^{-12}$. How far a split column
differs from one block on CPU and on GPU beyond these bounds is **not measured at the pin**. The header comment of
`test_pref_local_seam.cpp` says that `HydroImpl` restarts the scan in a second same-process block and that the test
does not fix it, while the assertions expect the relay of this section ({{< code tests/test_pref_local_seam.cpp >}});
the comment is stale against the code it tests. The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
